title: Statements and Assumptions
tagline: Year 2 — Finding the unstated premise on which a statement depends

introduction.overview: An assumption is something taken for granted by the speaker or writer, without being stated, which must be true for the statement to make sense. In an assumption question you are given a statement and two or more candidate assumptions, and you must pick those that are implicit. The test is: "If the assumption were false, would the statement become pointless or unreasonable?"
introduction.placementRelevance: Statements and assumptions questions are commonly asked in company reasoning rounds, mostly with advertisements, advice and announcements.
introduction.realWorldContext: Analysing an advertisement, a policy proposal or an argument in a meeting involves spotting the premises that its author takes for granted.

learningObjectives: Distinguish assumptions from conclusions and from restatements
Apply the "negation test" to check whether an assumption is necessary
Reject assumptions that are too strong, too general or unrelated
Recognise typical assumptions in advertisements, advice and announcements
Handle questions with one or two assumptions

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: A conclusion follows from a statement; an assumption lies behind it. A restatement is neither.

coreDefinitions: Assumption: an unstated belief that the speaker takes for granted, necessary for the statement to hold.
Negation test: if the opposite of the assumption makes the statement meaningless, the assumption is implicit.
Strong words (all, always, only, never, best) usually make an assumption invalid.
Advertisement assumption: "people want what is advertised" and "people will respond".
Advice assumption: the advice is useful and can be followed.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: People speak with background beliefs that they do not state. A shopkeeper who says "Buy our toothpaste for strong teeth" assumes people want strong teeth and that toothpaste can help. An assumption is such a hidden belief, necessary to make the statement sensible.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: For each assumption, flip it to its opposite and ask whether the statement would still make sense. If not, it is implicit. If the statement still works, the assumption is not necessary.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Negation test
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Negate the assumption; does the statement collapse?
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: "Lift is working" negated → advice to use the lift is pointless

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Strong-word filter
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Reject assumptions with all, always, only, never, best, everyone
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Too extreme to be taken for granted.
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: No other soap keeps skin fresh → reject

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Restatement filter
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: An assumption is not a repeat of the statement
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: "Her sister is getting married" repeated → not an assumption

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Cause-purpose rule
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: A statement about doing X to achieve Y assumes X can achieve Y

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Advertisement rule
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Ads assume people want the benefit and may respond

mainNarrative: Read the statement and ask: "What must the speaker believe for this to be a sensible thing to say?" In "Use the lift if you are going above the second floor", the speaker must believe the lift is working and available.

Apply the negation test to each candidate. If the lift were out of order, the advice would be pointless, so "the lift is working" is implicit. The candidate "People going above the second floor use only the stairs" is not necessary for the advice.
Reject extreme assumptions. "No other soap keeps the skin fresh" is too strong; an advertisement need not claim this. Likewise "all roads are jammed" is not needed to recommend the metro.

Reject restatements. If the statement says Rohit wants leave to attend his sister's wedding, "his sister is getting married" repeats the statement and is not an assumption. The assumption would be that such leave is likely to be approved.

Means-end statements ("do X to achieve Y") assume X helps achieve Y. A city that installs speed cameras to reduce accidents assumes that speeding contributes to accidents and that cameras deter speeding.

deepDiveAspects.title: Assumptions vs conclusions
deepDiveAspects.content: A conclusion is a consequence of the statement; an assumption is a precondition. Ask: does it come after (conclusion) or before (assumption)?

deepDiveAspects.title: Two good assumptions
deepDiveAspects.content: Sometimes both assumptions are valid. When the statement relies on two separate hidden beliefs, both pass the negation test.

problemVariations.exampleSnippet: Buy this toothpaste for strong teeth
Study at night because evenings are noisy

solvedExamples.title: Advice
solvedExamples.question: Statement: Please use the lift if you are going above the second floor. Assumptions: I. The lift is working. II. People going above the second floor use only the stairs.

steps.title: Assumption I
steps.explanation: If the lift is not working, the advice is pointless: implicit.

steps.title: Assumption II
steps.explanation: The advice does not rely on this: not implicit.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Advice presumes it can be followed.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Accepting II because it sounds related.

solvedExamples.title: Advertisement
solvedExamples.question: Statement: Use Brightmax toothpaste for strong teeth. Assumptions: I. People want strong teeth. II. Other toothpastes are harmful.

steps.title: Assumption I
steps.explanation: The ad assumes people want strong teeth: implicit.

steps.title: Assumption II
steps.explanation: Too strong, not required: not implicit.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: An advertisement does not need to claim rivals are harmful.

solvedExamples.title: Means and end
solvedExamples.question: Statement: To reduce accidents, the city has decided to install speed cameras. Assumptions: I. Speeding contributes to accidents. II. Speed cameras will deter speeding.

steps.title: Assumption I
steps.explanation: If speeding did not contribute, the plan would not reduce accidents: implicit.

steps.title: Assumption II
steps.explanation: If cameras did not deter, the plan would fail: implicit.

solvedExamples.finalAnswer: Both I and II are implicit
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Both are links in the chain from the decision to the goal.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Negate each candidate and ask if the statement still makes sense. Reject extreme, unrelated and restating candidates.

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Treating a result as an assumption.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Reject candidates with strong words first.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Apply the negation test to each.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Advertisements and advice are the most common.

easy.question:
Statement: Please use the lift if you are going above the second floor.
Assumptions: I. The lift is working. II. People going above the second floor use only the stairs.
Which of the following is correct?
options: Only assumption II is implicit
Only assumption I is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
easy.explanation: The advice presumes the lift is available. II is not needed.

easy.question:
Statement: Use Brightmax toothpaste for strong teeth.
Assumptions: I. People want strong teeth. II. Other toothpastes are harmful.
Which of the following is correct?
options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
easy.explanation: The advertisement presumes people want strong teeth. II is too strong.

easy.question:
Statement: The teacher said: "Read the chapter before coming to class."
Assumptions: I. Students have access to the chapter. II. The teacher will test the students.
Which of the following is correct?
options: Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
Only assumption I is implicit
easy.explanation: The instruction presumes access. A test is not necessary.

intermediate.question:
Statement: The government has increased bus fares, so people will shift to trains.
Assumptions: I. Train fares are lower than the new bus fares. II. People travel only by bus.
Which of the following is correct?
options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
intermediate.explanation: Shifting presumes trains are cheaper. II contradicts the shift.

intermediate.question:
Statement: Apply for the job on our website only.
Assumptions: I. Candidates have internet access. II. Applications by post are illegal.
Which of the following is correct?
options: Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
Only assumption I is implicit
intermediate.explanation: The instruction presumes online access. II is too strong.

intermediate.question:
Statement: A says to B: "Give me your phone; I will call him."
Assumptions: I. A's own phone is not available. II. B has a phone.
Which of the following is correct?
options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
intermediate.correctAnswer: Both I and II are implicit
intermediate.explanation: The request presumes A has no phone at hand and that B has one.

advanced.question:
Statement: To reduce accidents, the city has decided to install speed cameras.
Assumptions: I. Speeding contributes to accidents. II. Speed cameras will deter speeding.
Which of the following is correct?
options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
advanced.correctAnswer: Both I and II are implicit
advanced.explanation: Both links are necessary for the plan to reduce accidents.

advanced.question:
Statement: An advertisement: "Only 1000 units of this phone are available; hurry."
Assumptions: I. People tend to buy quickly if stock is limited. II. This phone is the best in the market.
Which of the following is correct?
options: Only assumption II is implicit
Only assumption I is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
advanced.explanation: The ad presumes scarcity prompts action. "Best" is not needed.

placementStyle.question:
Statement: The principal ordered that all mobile phones be switched off in class.
Assumptions: I. Phones can disturb the class. II. Phones are used for studying.
Which of the following is correct?
options: Only assumption II is implicit
Only assumption I is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
placementStyle.explanation: The order presumes phones can disturb. II is not needed.

placementStyle.question:
Statement: She turned off the AC to save electricity.
Assumptions: I. The AC consumes electricity. II. She is poor.
Which of the following is correct?
options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
placementStyle.explanation: The action presumes the AC uses electricity. II is irrelevant.

placementStyle.question:
Statement: Rohit applied for three days' leave to attend his sister's wedding.
Assumptions: I. Leave is likely to be granted for such a reason. II. Rohit's sister is getting married.
Which of the following is correct?
options: Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
Only assumption I is implicit
placementStyle.explanation: II restates the statement. The unstated assumption is that the leave may be granted.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I apply the negation test?
Can I reject an extreme assumption?
Can I find the means-end link?
